summary: Tether is a browser game where you design and fly a small satellite to carry one emergency message, typed by you, from a flood-cut community you choose to a relief station before a deadline. You pick a radio, a battery and an orbit within a $150k budget, then operate the mission: transmit only when the satellite passes overhead, manage power through eclipse, and survive a flooded ground station. The physics are simplified but real: orbital period, ground-track passes, free-space path loss and an energy budget. Every transmission shows clearly whether it was sent or failed and why, and every mission ends with a debrief explaining the chain of cause and effect. The core lesson: engineering decisions interact, and the most expensive build is not the best mission.
details:
What it does: the player types the community's emergency message, chooses a location anywhere from 55S to 55N, builds a satellite from a catalog of radios, batteries and orbits under a $150k budget, then flies it in real time. The message moves in two hops (store-and-forward): community to satellite during a pass, satellite to relief station during a later pass. Each transmission shows a clear sent or failed result with the reason. A scripted flood takes the relief station offline. Win by delivering before the deadline; lose and a debrief names the cause: energy, link, scheduling or disruption.

How it works: a pure TypeScript simulation models a 51.6 degree circular orbit, a 10 degree elevation mask, a 437 MHz UHF link budget (free-space path loss), solar charging with eclipse, radio standby and transmit loads, and a battery transmit floor. 25 automated tests across 8 cities verify the physics and the core lesson: the brute-force 25 W build runs dry, a matched 2 W build delivers.

Design for unhappy paths: polar locations are explained and blocked; near the equator the deadline stretches honestly instead of faking passes; over-budget builds cannot launch; an empty message cannot be sent; every failed transmission names its exact reason.

Tools: Vite, React, TypeScript, Vitest, Canvas 2D, deployed on Vercel. Brand assets from our designer's Canva kit. Code: https://github.com/agapemiteu/Tether

Impact: anyone with a browser can fly real mission trade-offs over their own home, and learn that engineering is trade-offs, not budgets.
